gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_mmio helper and survey reviewable without widening into a transport lifecycle claim.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, bounded queue descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the MMIO lane should build on that real foothold instead of inventing a second core starter.
The existing ring survey keeps the queue-wrapper roadmap gap explicit, which the MMIO lane depends on before transport-facing work can honestly begin.

The live repo now has a tiny in-memory virtqueue helper for queue shape, notification bookkeeping, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable state, and delayed-callback pacing, so the MMIO lane can add one bounded register-window helper against a real queue-facing foothold.

The live virtio_ring helper now already covers queue shape, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable, and delayed-callback pacing, which closes the last queue-local blocker ahead of the first MMIO wrapper step.

The live repo now ships one tiny in-memory MMIO register-window helper for aligned bounded reads, queue-select bookkeeping, queue-size programming, queue-ready state, status writes, and config-generation reads without claiming queue discovery, reset, or probe lifecycle behavior.

A dedicated MMIO helper gate keeps the new register-window wrapper reviewable through explicit bounds, read-only register protection, and queue-window selection checks before any interrupt or lifecycle follow-up.
A dedicated MMIO survey gate keeps the transport gap explicit and reviewable now that the first register-window helper is landed but broader transport behavior is still intentionally absent.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current MMIO helper surface and the reasons broader transport work is still blocked behind that first register-window foothold.
With the first register-window helper now landed, the next honest MMIO step is one tiny in-memory interrupt-status and acknowledgement helper before queue discovery, reset, or probe lifecycle work.

Full queue discovery, reset flows, interrupt delivery, and probe or remove lifecycle behavior remain too transport-facing to start honestly while the MMIO lane is still limited to bounded register-window helpers.
